Director of the Cyberspace Administration of China, Zhuang Rongwen Director of the State Administration for Market Regulation, Luo Wen October 14, 2025 Measures for the Authentication of Personal Information Outbound Transfer Article 1 For the purpose of protecting personal information rights and interests, regulating personal information outbound transfer authentication activities, and promoting efficient and secure cross-border flow of personal information, these Measures are formulated in accordance with the Personal Information Protection Law of the People's Republic of China, the Regulation on Network Data Security Management, the Certification and Accreditation Regulations of the People's Republic of China, and other relevant laws and regulations. Article 2 Personal information processors providing personal information to outside the territory of the People's Republic of China through the method of personal information protection certification shall be subject to these Measures. Article 4 The national cyberspace information department shall, together with the national data management department and other relevant departments, formulate standards and technical specifications related to personal information outbound transfer authentication. Measures for the Certification of Personal Information Crossing Borders | Art. 3 | :: Director of [Office] Zhuang Rongwen Director of the State Administration for Market Regulation Luo Wen October 14, 2025 Measures for the Certification of Personal Information Crossing Borders Article 1: In order to protect the rights and interests of personal information, standardize the certification activities for personal information crossing borders, and promote the efficient and secure cross-border flow of personal information, these Measures are formulated in accordance with the Personal Information Protection Law of the People's Republic of China, the Network Data Security Management Regulations, the Regulations on Certification and Accreditation of the People's Republic of China, and other relevant laws and regulations. Article 2: When a personal information processor provides personal information to outside the territory of the People's Republic of China by means of personal information protection certification, these Measures shall apply. Article 3: The personal information crossing border certification referred to in these Measures means the conformity assessment activity whereby a professional certification body that has lawfully obtained certification qualifications for personal information protection, in accordance with Article 38, Paragraph 1, Item 2 of the Personal Information Protection Law of the People's Republic of China, certifies that the personal information processing activities of the personal information processor in providing personal information to outside the territory of the People's Republic of China and other personal information processing activities comply with relevant laws, administrative regulations, departmental rules, standards, and technical specifications. Article 4: The national cyberspace administration department, together with the national data management department and other relevant departments, shall formulate relevant standards and technical specifications for personal information crossing border certification. The national market supervision and administration department, together with the national cyberspace administration department, shall formulate rules for personal information protection certification and establish unified certification certificates and marks. Article 5: When a personal information processor provides personal information to outside the territory by means of personal information crossing border certification, it shall simultaneously satisfy the following circumstances: (1) Is not an operator of critical information infrastructure; (2) Has cumulatively provided personal information of 100,000 or more but fewer than 1,000,000 persons (not including sensitive personal information) to outside the territory from January 1 of the current year.

The risk assessment report shall include the following contents: (1) Basic information of the network data processor, information of the network data security management organization, the name and contact information of the person in charge of network data security, and so forth; (2) The purpose, type, quantity, method, scope, storage period, storage location and other matters relating to the processing of important data, the situation of network data processing activities conducted, not including the content of network data itself; (3) The network data security management system and its implementation situation, technical measures such as encryption, backup, labeling and marking, access control, security authentication and other necessary measures and their effectiveness; (4) Network data security risks discovered, network data security incidents that have occurred and their handling situation; (5) The risk assessment situation regarding provision of, entrustment to process, or joint processing of important data; (6) The situation of network data crossing borders; (7) Other reporting contents stipulated by competent departments. A risk assessment report submitted by a large-scale network platform service provider processing important data shall, in addition to including the contents stipulated in the preceding paragraph, also fully explain the situation regarding critical business and supply chain network data security. Where a processor of important data engages in important data processing activities that may endanger national security, competent departments at or above provincial level shall order it to adopt measures for rectification or cessation of processing important data. The processor of important data shall immediately adopt measures in accordance with the relevant requirements. Chapter V Cross-Border Network Data Security Administration Article 34 The national cyberspace administration department shall, in coordination with relevant departments, establish a specialized working mechanism for national data cross-border security administration, develop and formulate policies related to national network data cross-border security administration, and coordinate the handling of major matters relating to network data cross-border security. Article 35 Where any of the following conditions is satisfied, a network data processor may provide personal information to foreign parties: (1) Passing the data cross-border security assessment organized by the national cyberspace administration department; (2) Having obtained personal information protection certification from a professional institution according to the regulations of the national cyberspace administration department; (3) Conforming to the provisions of the standard contract concerning personal information cross-border transmission formulated by the national cyberspace administration department;

Providers of network products and services shall continuously provide security maintenance for their products and services; they shall not terminate the provision of security maintenance within the period prescribed or agreed upon by the parties. Providers of network products and services shall continue to provide security maintenance for their products and services; within the period prescribed or agreed upon by the parties, they shall not terminate the provision of security maintenance. Network operators shall adopt measures as required, carry out rectification, and eliminate hazards. Article 59: Where a network security incident causes the occurrence of an emergency event or production safety accident, it shall be handled in accordance with the provisions of the relevant laws and administrative regulations such as the Law of the People's Republic of China on Emergency Response to Unexpected Events and the Law of the People's Republic of China on Work Safety

REGULATIONS ON THE SECURITY PROTECTION OF CRITICAL INFORMATION INFRASTRUCTURE | Art. 3 | Chapter One General Provisions, p.1 :: REGULATIONS ON THE SECURITY PROTECTION OF CRITICAL INFORMATION INFRASTRUCTURE CHAPTER ONE GENERAL PROVISIONS Article 1: In order to safeguard the security of critical information infrastructure, maintain network security, and in accordance with the Cybersecurity Law of the People's Republic of China, these Regulations are formulated. Article 2: The critical information infrastructure referred to in these Regulations means the important network facilities, information systems and other such facilities in important industries and sectors including public communications and information services, energy, transportation, water conservancy, finance, public services, e-government, and national defense science and technology industries, which, once destroyed, lose function, or experience data disclosure, may seriously endanger national security, national economy and people's livelihood, or public interests. Article 3: Under the overall coordination of the national cyberspace administration department, the State Council public security department shall be responsible for guiding and supervising the security protection work of critical information infrastructure. The State Council telecommunications authority and other relevant departments shall, in accordance with the provisions of these Regulations and relevant laws and administrative regulations, within the scope of their respective responsibilities, be responsible for the security protection and supervision and management work of critical information infrastructure. The relevant departments of provincial-level people's governments shall, in accordance with their respective responsibilities, implement security protection and supervision and management of critical information infrastructure. Article 4: The security protection of critical information infrastructure shall adhere to the principles of comprehensive coordination, division of responsibility, and protection in accordance with law, strengthen and implement the principal responsibility of critical information infrastructure operators (hereinafter referred to as operators), give full play to the role of government and all sectors of society, and jointly protect the security of critical information infrastructure. Article 5: The State shall implement priority protection of critical information infrastructure, take measures to monitor, defend against, and handle cybersecurity risks and threats from sources both within and outside the territory of the People's Republic of China, protect critical information infrastructure from attack, intrusion, interference and destruction, and lawfully punish unlawful and criminal acts that endanger the security of critical information infrastructure.

Chapter II - Identification of Critical Information Infrastructure Article 8 The competent departments and supervisory management departments of the important industries and sectors referred to in Article 2 of these Regulations are the departments responsible for the work of protecting critical information infrastructure security (hereinafter referred to as "protection work departments"). Article 10 Protection work departments shall, in accordance with the identification rules, be responsible for organizing the identification of critical information infrastructure in their respective industries and sectors, promptly notify operators of the identification results, and report to the State Council Public Security Department. Article 11 Where critical information infrastructure undergoes significant changes that may affect its identification result, operators shall promptly report the relevant situation to the protection work department. The protection work department shall complete a re-identification within 3 months from the date of receipt of the report, notify the operator of the identification result, and report to the State Council Public Security Department. Chapter III - Operator Responsibilities and Obligations Article 12 Security protection measures shall be consistent with critical information infrastructure

Measures for Data Security Management in the Industrial and Information Technology Sector (Trial Implementation) (gov.cn) | Art. 13 | Chapter III Data Security Management Throughout the Full Lifecycle If requirements are met, registration shall be granted, and the registration situation shall simultaneously be reported to the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology; if registration is not granted, timely feedback shall be provided to the registration applicant with an explanation of the reasons. The registration applicant shall resubmit the registration application within fifteen working days after receiving the feedback. Where there are major changes in the content of registration, data processors in the industrial and information technology sector shall complete the registration change procedures within three months of the change occurring. Major changes refer to changes of 30% or more in the scale of certain types of important data and core data (number of data entries or total storage volume, etc.), or changes in other registration contents. Chapter III Data Security Management Throughout the Full Lifecycle Article 13 Data processors in the industrial and information technology sector shall bear the security principal responsibility for data processing activities, implement tiered protection for all categories of data. Where different levels of data are processed simultaneously and it is difficult to adopt protective measures separately, protection shall be implemented in accordance with the requirements of the highest level among them, ensuring that data remains continuously in a state of effective protection and lawful use. (1) Establish a data security management system covering the full lifecycle, and formulate specific tiered protection requirements and operational procedures for data processing activities at different levels, including data collection, storage, use, processing, transmission, provision, and public disclosure; (2) Configure data security management personnel as necessary to comprehensively oversee security supervision and management of data processing activities, and assist industry regulatory departments in carrying out their work; (3) Reasonably determine operational authority for data processing activities and strictly implement personnel authority management; (4) Formulate emergency response plans as needed to address data security incidents, and conduct emergency drills; (5) Regularly conduct data security education and training for employees; (6) Other measures as provided for by laws, administrative regulations, and so forth. Data processors handling important data and core data in the industrial and information technology sector shall additionally: (1) Establish a data security work system covering relevant departments of the organization, clarify the data security officer and management institution, and establish a normalized mechanism for communication and coordination. The legal representative or principal responsible person of the organization is the first responsible person for data security, and the team member with responsibility for data security is the directly responsible person; (2) Clarify key positions for data processing and position responsibilities, and require key position personnel to sign a data security responsibility letter. The responsibility letter shall include but not be limited to the content of data security position responsibilities, obligations, disciplinary measures, precautions, and other matters; (3) Establish internal registration, approval, and other working mechanisms, implement strict management of important data and core data processing activities, and retain records. Article 14 Data processors in the industrial and information technology sector shall follow the principles of lawfulness and propriety when collecting data and shall not steal or collect data by other illegal means. During the data collection process, corresponding security measures shall be adopted according to the data security level. The management of personnel and equipment engaged in collecting important data and core data shall be strengthened, and records shall be kept of the collection sources, time, types, quantities, frequencies, and flows. Where important data and core data are obtained through indirect channels, data processors in the industrial and information technology sector shall, through signing relevant agreements, commitment letters, and other means with the data provider, clarify the legal responsibilities of both parties.

Regulations on Network Data Security Management | Art. 31 | Chapter Four: Important Data Security :: Supervise network data security risks and incidents; (3) Accept and handle network data security complaints and reports. The network data security officer shall possess professional knowledge of network data security and relevant management work experience, and shall be assumed by members of the management layer of the network data processor, and has the right to directly report network data security conditions to relevant competent departments. Network data processors that master specific categories and scales of important data as prescribed by relevant competent departments shall conduct security background reviews of network data security officers and personnel in key positions, and strengthen training of relevant personnel. During the review, application may be made to public security organs and national security organs for assistance. Article 31: Before a processor of important data provides, entrusts the processing of, or jointly processes important data, it shall conduct a risk assessment; however, this does not apply where it is performed to fulfill statutory duties or legal obligations. Risk assessment shall focus on assessing the following contents: (1) Whether the purpose, manner, scope and other aspects of providing, entrusting the processing of, or jointly processing network data, as well as the network data receiver's processing of network data, are lawful, proper, and necessary; (2) The risks of network data being tampered with, destroyed, leaked, or illegally obtained or illegally used, and the risks brought to national security, public interests, or the legitimate rights and interests of individuals or organizations; (3) The integrity, law-abidingness and other circumstances of the network data receiver; (4) Whether the requirements regarding network data security in contracts entered into or to be entered into with the network data receiver can effectively constrain the network data receiver in fulfilling its obligations to protect network data security; (5) Whether the technical and management measures adopted or to be adopted can effectively prevent the risks of network data being tampered with, destroyed, leaked, or illegally obtained, illegally used, and the like; (6) Other assessment contents as prescribed by relevant competent departments. Article 32: Where a processor of important data undergoes merger, division, dissolution, bankruptcy, or other circumstances that may affect the security of important data, it shall take measures to safeguard network data security, and report to provincial-level or above competent departments the disposal plan for important data, the name or personal name of the receiver, and contact information; where the competent department is unclear, it shall report to the provincial-level or above data security work coordination mechanism. Article 33: A processor of important data shall conduct a risk assessment of its network data processing activities on an annual basis, and submit a risk assessment report to provincial-level or above competent departments, which shall promptly notify network information departments at the same level.

Article 10: No unit or individual shall engage in money laundering activities or provide convenience for money laundering activities, and shall cooperate with financial institutions and specific non-financial institutions in carrying out customer due diligence in accordance with law. Article 11: Any unit or individual discovering money laundering activities has the right to report to the anti-money laundering administrative authorities, public security organs, or other relevant state organs.

Article 38: When conducting audits, audited units shall not transfer, conceal, alter, or destroy financial and accounting records, or materials related to government financial revenue and expenditure and financial revenue and expenditure, including business and management materials; audited units shall not transfer, conceal, or intentionally damage assets obtained in violation of state regulations. Where audited units violate the provisions of the preceding paragraph, audit agencies have the right to order cessation; where necessary, with approval from the principal of a county-level or higher-level people's government audit agency, audit agencies have the right to seal relevant materials and assets obtained in violation of state regulations; where deposits of the aforementioned kind at financial institutions require freezing, application shall be made to the people's court.

Article 28: The Internet Information Content Management Department shall, within seven days, make the following disposition decisions regarding evidence that has been preliminarily registered and preserved: (1) Where evidence preservation measures are required, evidence preservation measures such as recording, copying, photographing, and video recording shall be taken before return; (2) Where inspection, testing, or appraisal is required, the materials shall be sent to institutions with the corresponding qualifications for inspection, testing, or appraisal; (3) Where unlawful facts are established, and confiscation is legally required, an administrative penalty decision shall be made and the unlawful items shall be confiscated; (4) Where unlawful facts are not established, or where unlawful facts are established but confiscation is not legally required, the preliminary registration and preservation shall be lifted.

MINISTRY OF PUBLIC SECURITY ORDER No. 82 "Provisions on Technical Measures for Internet Security Protection" has been approved at the Office Meeting of the Minister of Public Security on November 23, 2005, and is hereby promulgated for implementation as of March 1, 2006. December 13, 2005 PROVISIONS ON TECHNICAL MEASURES FOR INTERNET SECURITY PROTECTION Article 1: In order to strengthen and standardize Internet security technical prevention work, safeguard Internet network security and information security, promote the healthy and orderly development of the Internet, and maintain national security, social order and public interests, these Provisions are formulated in accordance with the "Administrative Measures for the Security Protection of International Networking of Computer Information Networks." Article 2: The Internet security protection technical measures referred to in these Provisions mean the technical facilities and technical methods for safeguarding Internet network security and information security and preventing illegal and criminal activities. Article 3: Internet service providers and networked user units shall be responsible for implementing Internet security protection technical measures and shall ensure the normal functioning of Internet security protection technical measures. Article 4: Internet service providers and networked user units shall establish corresponding management systems. Without the consent of users, the registered information of users shall not be made public or leaked, except where otherwise provided by law or regulation. Internet service providers and networked user units shall use Internet security protection technical measures in accordance with law and shall not use Internet security protection technical measures to infringe upon users' freedom of communication and confidentiality of communication. Article 5: The public security apparatus' department for public information network security supervision shall be responsible for lawfully implementing supervision and management of the implementation of Internet security protection technical measures. Article 6: Internet security protection technical measures shall comply with national standards. Where national standards do not exist, they shall comply with public safety industry technical standards. Article 7: Internet service providers and networked user units shall implement the following Internet security protection technical measures: (1) Technical measures to prevent computer viruses, network intrusions and attack damage and other matters or acts that endanger network security; (2) Redundant disaster recovery and backup measures for important databases and major equipment of systems; (3) Technical measures to record and retain user login and logout times, calling numbers, account numbers, Internet addresses or domain names, and system maintenance logs; (4) Other security protection technical measures as provided by law, regulation and rules. Article 8: Units providing Internet access services shall, in addition to implementing the Internet security protection technical measures specified in Article 7 of these Provisions, also implement security protection technical measures with the following functions: (1) Record and retain user registration information; (2) For units providing access services through the conversion method of internal network addresses and Internet network addresses, be able to record and retain the correspondence relationship between the Internet network addresses and internal network addresses used by users; (3) Record and track network operation status, monitor and record network security events and other security audit functions. Article 9: Units providing Internet information services shall, in addition to implementing the Internet security protection technical measures specified in Article 7 of these Provisions, also implement security protection technical measures with the following functions: (1) Discover and stop the transmission of illegal information in public information services, and retain relevant records; (2) For units providing news, publishing and electronic bulletin board services, be able to record and retain the content of published information and the time of publication; (3) For units operating portal websites, news websites and electronic commerce websites, be able to prevent websites and web pages from being tampered with, and automatically recover after tampering; (4) For units operating electronic bulletin board services, possess user registration information and published information audit functions; (5) For units operating electronic mail and online short message services, be able to prevent and eliminate electronic mail or short messages sent in batch mode that forge or conceal the true identification marks of the information sender. Article 10: Units providing Internet data center services and networked user units shall, in addition to implementing the Internet security protection technical measures specified in Article 7 of these Provisions, also implement security protection technical measures with the following functions: (1) Record and retain user registration information; (2) Discover and stop the transmission of illegal information in public information services, and retain relevant records; (3) For networked user units that provide access services to users through the conversion method of internal network addresses and Internet network addresses, be able to record and retain the correspondence relationship between the Internet network addresses and internal network addresses used by users. Article 11: Units providing Internet access services for the public shall, in addition to implementing the Internet security protection technical measures specified in Article 7 of these Provisions, also install and operate the security management system for Internet public access service places. Article 12: Internet service providers shall ensure that the Internet security protection technical measures adopted in accordance with these Provisions have networked interfaces that comply with public safety industry technical standards. Article 13: Internet service providers and networked user units shall ensure that the record retention technical measures implemented in accordance with these Provisions possess the function of retaining backups of records for at least 60 days. Article 14: Internet service providers and networked user units shall not implement the following acts of destroying Internet security protection technical measures: (1) Arbitrarily cease or partially cease the operation of security protection technical facilities or technical means; (2) Intentionally damage security protection technical facilities; (3) Arbitrarily delete or tamper with the operation programs and records of security protection technical facilities or technical means; (4) Arbitrarily change the purpose and scope of security protection technical measures; (5) Other acts of intentionally destroying security protection technical measures or obstructing their normal functioning. Article 15: Those who violate Articles 7 through 14 of these Provisions shall be punished by the public security apparatus in accordance with the provisions of Article 21 of the "Administrative Measures for the Security Protection of International Networking of Computer Information Networks." Chapter Seven Supervision and Management Article 47 The national cyberspace administration department shall be responsible for overall coordination of network data security and related supervision and management work. Public security organs and national security organs shall, in accordance with relevant laws, administrative regulations and the provisions of these regulations, undertake network data security supervision and management responsibilities within their respective scope of duties, and shall in accordance with law prevent and crack down on illegal and criminal activities endangering network data security. Within ten working days from the date of receipt of a risk assessment report, they shall notify the network information department at the same level. With respect to the same network data security incident or risk, no repeated requests shall be made for a network data processor to engage an assessment institution to conduct a risk assessment. Article 18 When a network data processor, pursuant to the requirements of the relevant departments, engages an assessment institution to conduct a risk assessment, it shall perform the following obligations: (1) Provide necessary support for the assessment institution to conduct the risk assessment, including providing assessment personnel with necessary access rights to network data facilities, network data, systems and operation log records, etc.; (2) Complete the risk assessment within the prescribed time period; where circumstances are complex, the time period may be appropriately extended with the approval of the relevant departments; (3) After completion of the risk assessment, submit the risk assessment report issued by the assessment institution to the relevant departments. The risk assessment report shall be signed and sealed by the principal person in charge of the assessment institution and the risk assessment personnel.

The competent securities supervision and management institution of the State Council shall compare and verify the relevant data concerning customers' transaction settlement funds, entrusted funds, and funds and securities in customers' guarantee accounts reported by relevant institutions, and shall promptly discover any situations in which funds or securities are unlawfully utilized. Article 66 - Securities companies shall, in accordance with law, make public disclosure to society of their basic information, shareholding and controlling situations, liabilities and contingent liabilities, business management conditions, financial income and expenditure conditions, compensation of senior management personnel, and other relevant information. The specific measures shall be formulated by the competent securities supervision and management institution of the State Council. Article 67 - The competent securities supervision and management institution of the State Council may require the following units or individuals to provide materials and information related to the business management and financial condition of securities companies within a designated time limit: (1) Securities companies and their directors, supervisors, and staff members; (2) Shareholders and actual controllers of securities companies; (3) Enterprises controlled by or actually controlled by securities companies; (4) Opening banks of securities companies, designated commercial banks, asset custody institutions, securities exchanges, and securities registration and settlement institutions; (5) Securities service institutions that provide services to securities companies. Article 68 - The competent securities supervision and management institution of the State Council has the authority to adopt the following measures to inspect the business activities, financial condition, and business management situation of securities companies: (1) Interrogate directors, supervisors, and staff members of securities companies and require them to provide explanations concerning relevant inspection matters; (2) Enter the office premises or business premises of securities companies for inspection; (3) Review and copy files and materials related to inspection matters; for files, materials, and electronic devices that may be transferred, concealed, or destroyed, take measures to seal them; (4) Inspect the computer information management systems of securities companies and copy relevant data and materials.

Regulation on Supervision and Management of Non-bank Payment Institutions | Art. 39 | Chapter IV Supervision and Management, p.1 :: Non-bank payment institutions of business types, except where the State has other provisions. Article 37 Non-bank payment institutions shall, in accordance with provisions, submit to the People's Bank of China payment business information, audited financial accounting reports, operational data statements, statistical data, and other materials related to corporate governance and business operations as required by the People's Bank of China. Article 38 The People's Bank of China shall, in accordance with provisions, conduct classification and rating of non-bank payment institutions, and implement classified supervision and management based on the results of classification and rating. The People's Bank of China shall, in accordance with law, formulate identification standards and supervision and management rules for systemically important non-bank payment institutions. Article 39 The People's Bank of China shall, in accordance with law, perform its duties and has the power to adopt the following measures: (1) conduct on-site inspections and off-site supervision and management of non-bank payment institutions; (2) enter locations where suspected unlawful and irregular conduct has occurred to investigate and collect evidence; (3) inquire of the parties and units and individuals related to the investigated matter, and require them to provide explanations regarding matters related to the investigated matter; (4) review and copy relevant documents, materials and business systems of the parties and units and individuals related to the investigated matter; with respect to documents, materials and business systems that may be transferred, concealed or destroyed, such documents, materials and business systems may be sealed or detained; (5) with approval from the responsible person of the People's Bank of China or its provincial-level branch, query account information of the parties and units and individuals related to the investigated matter. In order to prevent risks and maintain market order, the People's Bank of China may adopt measures such as ordering corrections, supervisory talks, issuing warning letters, and releasing risk alerts to the public. Article 40 The People's Bank of China shall, in accordance with law, perform its duties and conduct on-site inspections or investigations; the personnel conducting on-site inspections and investigations shall be no fewer than 2 persons, and shall present lawful certificates and law enforcement documents. Where the personnel conducting on-site inspections and investigations are fewer than 2 persons or have not presented lawful certificates and law enforcement documents, the inspected or investigated units and individuals have the right to refuse. The People's Bank of China shall, in accordance with law, perform its duties; the inspected or investigated units and individuals shall cooperate and truthfully provide relevant documents, materials and business systems, and shall not refuse, obstruct or conceal. Article 41 - Where a non-bank payment institution experiences matters that have a material impact on its operational development, the stability and continuity of payment business, and the legitimate rights and interests of users, it shall report to the People's Bank of China in accordance with regulations. Where the principal shareholders of a non-bank payment institution intend to pledge shares of the non-bank payment institution, they shall report to the People's Bank of China in accordance with regulations; the pledged shares shall not exceed 50% of the total shares held by such shareholder in the non-bank payment institution. Article 42 - Non-bank payment institutions shall not engage in monopolistic or unfair competitive conduct that impairs the order of fair market competition.
